title: Degree-zero comparison over a strictly henselian base
statement:
Let $A$ be strictly henselian local
[def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and write
$k=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $s$ be the *canonical closed geometric point*
$s:\Spec k^{\mathrm{alg}}\to S$ with $k^{\mathrm{alg}}$ an algebraic closure
of $k$ (the convention of this statement; by Stacks Lemma 0A3I the sections of the
pullback of an etale sheaf do not change under a further extension of the
separably closed field $k^{\mathrm{alg}}$, so this normalization is a convention and
not a restriction), and let $p:Z\to S$ be proper
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every etale sheaf $F$ on the small
etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $Z$, restriction gives

$$
 \Gamma(Z,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Z_s,F|_{Z_s}),
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\quad
 \Gamma(Z,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Z_0,F|_{Z_0})
$$

with $Z_0=Z\times_S\Spec k$ (the identification of $Z_s$ with $Z_0$ being the
universal homeomorphism of the proof). This isomorphism is natural in $F$ and
in finite pullback over $S$.

proof.text: Put $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $Z_0=Z\times_SS_0$, and $i_0:Z_0\to Z$. Since $A$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a henselian pair and $k$ is separably closed. The proper map $p:Z\to S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the affine $S$, so $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. For any finite $h:Z'\to Z$, the composite $p\circ h:Z'\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (c). Its closed fibre is $Z'_0=Z'\times_SS_0=Z'\times_ZZ_0$ by associativity of fibre products.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0C (lemma-h0-proper-over-henselian-pair), lines 18200-18210; this item specializes I to the maximal ideal and compares the closed fibre with its algebraic-closure geometric fibre

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-h0-proper-henselian-pair] to $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and $p$. For every Zariski sheaf of sets $G$ on $Z$, restriction $\Gamma(Z,G)\to\Gamma(Z_0,i_0^{-1}G)$ is bijective. Apply the same node to each proper composite $p\circ h$ of Step 1. For every finite $h:Z'\to Z$ and every Zariski sheaf of sets $G'$ on $Z'$, restriction to $Z'_0=Z'\times_ZZ_0$ is bijective. These are exactly the two Zariski hypotheses of the finite-cover criterion, for the single closed immersion $i_0$ and all its finite base changes.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0C (lemma-h0-proper-over-henselian-pair), lines 18200-18210; this item specializes I to the maximal ideal and compares the closed fibre with its algebraic-closure geometric fibre

proof.text: The scheme $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by Step 1, and $i_0:Z_0\to Z$ is a closed immersion because it is the base change of $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)\to S$ (as in the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-h0-proper-henselian-pair]). Thus the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-h0-etale-criterion] are Step 2, and its conclusion applies to every etale sheaf of sets $F$ on $Z$: $\Gamma(Z,F)\to\Gamma(Z_0,i_{0,\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$ is bijective. This is the closed-fibre comparison of Stacks Tag 0A0C; the criterion is its cited Tag 09ZF.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0C (lemma-h0-proper-over-henselian-pair), lines 18200-18210; this item specializes I to the maximal ideal and compares the closed fibre with its algebraic-closure geometric fibre

proof.text: Let $K=k^{\mathrm{alg}}$. The algebraic extension $K/k$ is purely inseparable: [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] says that $K$ is purely inseparable over the relative separable closure of $k$ in $K$, and that closure is $k$ because $k$ is separably closed (Step 1). For every $k$-scheme $T$, [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] makes $T_K\to T$ a homeomorphism. Taking every $T$ proves that $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]; its base change $u:Z_s=Z_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z_0$ is one by [lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change]. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], inverse image along $u$ is an equivalence of small etale topoi, so its induced map on sections $\Gamma(Z_0,i_0^{-1}F)\to\Gamma(Z_s,u^{-1}i_0^{-1}F)$ is bijective. Since $u^{-1}i_0^{-1}F=F|_{Z_s}$ by functoriality of inverse image, composing with Step 3 gives the displayed geometric-fibre comparison.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0C (lemma-h0-proper-over-henselian-pair), specialized to the maximal ideal; geometric-fibre passage via the purely inseparable extension and topological invariance, Tag 04DY

proof.text: Every map in Steps 3 and 4 is the canonical restriction or inverse-image map. For a morphism $F\to F'$, the two restriction squares commute because inverse image is a functor [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For a finite $h:Z'\to Z$ over $S$, the square of the two closed-fibre restrictions commutes by the closed-fibre equation in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pullback-identities]; the geometric-fibre square is its base change to $K$. Both comparison maps are bijections by Steps 1-4 applied also to $Z'$, so their inverse isomorphisms have the same naturality. This proves the final clause.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be strictly henselian local, let
$h:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper, and let $T_0$ be the closed
geometric fibre. For every etale sheaf of sets $E$ on $T$, restriction is a
bijection

$$
\Gamma(T,E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T_0,E|_{T_0}).
$$

The bijection is functorial in $E$ and in finite morphisms over $T$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
We first prove the corresponding assertion for Zariski sheaves, uniformly
after every finite $T'\to T$. The space $T'$ is spectral and $T'\to \operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper. For an irreducible closed reduced
$C\subset T'$, Stein factorization gives

$$
C\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Spec}A,
$$

where $A\to B$ is integral and the first map has geometrically connected
fibres. The pair $(B,\mathfrak mB)$ is henselian: an idempotent of a finite
$B$-algebra modulo $\mathfrak m$ satisfies $e^2-e=0$, and the simple roots
$0,1$ lift uniquely by the henselian property of $A$ after restriction of
scalars along the integral algebra $B$. Consequently the closed subset
$\operatorname{Spec}B\cap V(\mathfrak m)$ is connected and nonempty. Its
inverse image $C\cap T'_0$ is connected because the map is closed,
surjective onto its image, and has connected fibres.

For completeness, let $G$ be a Zariski sheaf on $T'$. Every point
specializes to $T'_0$, so a global section is determined by its restriction.
For existence, write $G$ as the filtered union of subsheaves generated by
finitely many sections on quasi-compact opens. Such a finitely generated
subsheaf embeds into a finite product
$\prod_b(i_b)_*\underline{M_b}$, where $i_b:C_b\hookrightarrow T'$ is
closed and $M_b$ is a finite set: take the finitely many values of the
generators and separate their equalizer loci. Sections of
$(i_b)_*\underline{M_b}$ are locally constant maps $C_b\to M_b$.
Connectedness of every $C\cap T'_0$ says that the connected components of
$C_b$ and $C_b\cap T'_0$ correspond, so such maps extend uniquely. Finite
products, intersections with the embedded subsheaf, and filtered colimits
preserve this equality of section sets. Thus
$\Gamma(T',G)=\Gamma(T'_0,G|)$ for every Zariski sheaf and every finite
$T'\to T$.

Now let $E$ be an etale sheaf. The map from the restriction to the Zariski
site followed by closed-fibre inverse image to the Zariski restriction of
$E|_{T_0}$ is stalkwise injective. Indeed, an elementary etale
neighbourhood $V\to T$ whose closed fibre has a local section has open image
$V_0\subset T$, and $V\to V_0$ is an etale cover; hence

$$
E(V_0)\longrightarrow E(V)
\rightrightarrows E(V\times_{V_0}V)
$$

is an equalizer. Taking the colimit over such neighbourhoods proves the
stalkwise injection. The Zariski result therefore proves injectivity of
$\Gamma(T,E)\to\Gamma(T_0,E|)$, and the same argument applies after every
finite $T'\to T$.

For surjectivity, take $t_0\in\Gamma(T_0,E|)$. By the definition of inverse
image and sheafification there are finitely many etale maps $V_a\to T_0$
covering $T_0$, etale $U_a\to T$, maps $V_a\to U_a\times_TT_0$, and
sections $s_a\in E(U_a)$ representing $t_0|_{V_a}$. Shrink $U_a$ to the
open image of $V_a$ in $U_a\times_TT_0$ and then in $U_a$; the sheaf
equalizer shows that $s_a|_{U_a\times_TT_0}=t_0|_{U_a\times_TT_0}$. Every
nonempty closed subset of $T$ meets $T_0$ by the connectedness argument
above, so $\coprod_aU_a\to T$ is surjective.

Choose the finite surjective refinement $r:T'\to T$ of the preceding lemma
and opens $W_a\subset T'$ mapping to $U_a$. Pulling back $s_a$ gives local
sections on $W_a$. On $W_a\cap W_b$ their closed-fibre restrictions both
equal $r_0^{-1}t_0$; the already proved injectivity for the finite scheme
$T'\to T$ makes them equal. They glue to $s'\in\Gamma(T',r^{-1}E)$.
The two pullbacks of $s'$ to $T'\times_TT'$ have the same closed-fibre
restriction, and injectivity for the finite morphism
$T'\times_TT'\to T$ makes them equal.

It remains to spell out descent along $r$, which need not be etale. At a
geometric point $\bar x\to T$, choose a geometric $\bar x'\to T'$ above it.
The germ of $s'$ at $\bar x'$ is an element of the stalk $E_{\bar x}$.
The equalizer equality on $T'\times_TT'$ makes this element independent of
$\bar x'$. Represent it on an etale neighbourhood of $\bar x$ in $T$.
After shrinking, its pullback equals $s'$ near every point over $\bar x$;
finiteness of $r$ makes that inverse image quasi-compact, so one shrinking
works for all of them. These local descended sections agree on overlaps
because equality can be checked at geometric stalks, and hence glue to
$s\in\Gamma(T,E)$. Its restriction is $t_0$ by injectivity on $T_0$.
All pullbacks used are the functorial sheafification units, so the argument
also proves functoriality in $E$ and compatibility with finite pullback. The
source locators are Tags `09ZG` and `09ZF`; neither is used as
an unexpanded conclusion.
